comments.body:
Investigation narrative moved out of the description (the plan-review admission cap is 8000 chars). The original filing, verbatim:

## Context

Discovered while root-causing `dewy-rotatable-tarsier` (d240). It is NOT that bug's root cause —
that is sync MCP tool bodies blocking the event loop — but it is a real, separate defect surfaced
by the same investigation, so it is filed rather than folded in.

## The defect

`/health` returning 200 does not establish that the container can serve an MCP request, yet it is
the ONLY thing the blue-green cutover waits for.

- `/health` is a FastMCP `custom_route` registered DELIBERATELY outside `RequireAuthMiddleware` and
  outside the DNS-rebinding transport-security guard (`src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:210-224`), so a 200
  exercises none of: the auth middleware, the transport-security host/origin guard,
  `ProxyAuthMiddleware`, the StreamableHTTP session manager, or the MCP handshake.
- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:794-798` polls `GET http://127.0.0.1:<newport>/health` until 200 and
  then flips the nginx upstream (`autodeploy.sh:835`). **The deploy path never issues a single
  `/mcp` request.** A container is promoted to live traffic having never proven it can serve one.

Measured on the box (2026-08-28): container started 20:21:23.80, uvicorn bound 20:21:29.00, first
`/health` 200 at 20:21:29.87, cutover logged at 20:21:30, and the container did not serve its first
`/mcp` request until **20:22:24** — 54 seconds after it was declared healthy and put in front of
traffic.

## Why it matters

A container whose `REBAR_MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS` does not admit the public hostname answers
`/health` 200 while returning **421 Invalid Host header** to every real request. Verified
in-process: driving an `initialize` through the session manager with a Host outside the allowlist
returns 421 in under a millisecond, while `/health` on the same server returns 200. The deploy would
promote that container and log "mcp redeployed + healthy". The same is true of an auth
misconfiguration.

Related: during the 5.5-7.5 s of Python process startup BEFORE uvicorn binds (measured across three
deploys: 5.20 s / 7.54 s / 5.49 s), the published host port is ALREADY bound by docker-proxy, so an
arriving connection is accepted and then hangs or is reset rather than being refused. Blue-green
shields autodeploy-driven deploys from that window, but `--restart always` (`autodeploy.sh:377`)
does not: a container that crashes restarts in place on the port nginx is currently pointing at,
with no health gate involved at all.

## This is a known class in this repo

`store_status`'s docstring (`_mcp_health.py:118-129`) and its pinning test
(`tests/unit/test_mcp_health_store_status.py`) record that `/health` used to report only
`in_flight`, so a container with NO ticket store passed both the container HEALTHCHECK and the
blue-green readiness gate, and a deployed server answered every tracker query as though the store
were empty for weeks (bugs `kilted-nuclear-bronco` / `mobile-groovy-badger`). The established
invariant is that `/health` must carry enough signal for the readiness gate to be meaningful. The
MCP request path — the only thing the container exists to serve — is still unrepresented in it.

## Suggested shape (not yet designed in detail)

Drive one real `initialize` through the server's own `StreamableHTTPSessionManager` during ASGI
lifespan startup, using a Host drawn from the server's own transport-security allowlist, and report
`{ok, status, elapsed_ms}` as a `handshake` field on `/health` beside `in_flight` and `store`.
Because uvicorn completes lifespan startup before it accepts connections, a later `/health` 200 then
proves by construction that this container has already served an MCP handshake. A working prototype
exists: it returns 200 in ~1 ms for a correctly configured server and 421 for a bad host allowlist.
The ASGI `receive` must yield the body once and then `http.disconnect` — without that the SSE
response stream never terminates and the drive hangs (observed).

Should follow d240's fix, not precede it: while sync tool bodies still occupy the event loop,
`/health` is unanswerable during any long tool call anyway (observed: `FailingStreak: 19`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A correctly configured server reports a successful startup handshake on `/health`.
- [ ] A server whose transport-security host allowlist does not admit its own probe reports the
      handshake as failed with the refusing status, instead of reporting ready.
- [ ] The handshake never raises and never hangs: a drive exceeding its budget is reported as a
      failure and boot continues.
- [ ] The handshake completes inside the ASGI lifespan, before uvicorn accepts its first connection.

comments.body:
Implemented and pushed for review as Gerrit change 2362 (commit 6598b34be0bc,
https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2362).

Plan-review gate: PASS + signed attestation on the 4th review run; claimed without any force
override. The three blocking findings the gate caught were all real and all changed the design:

1. G6 — mirroring autodeploy step 5b verbatim would have copied its `record_backoff_failure`
   (the REVIEW-BOT recorder, which writes $BACKOFF_FILE and gates the whole script). The new gate
   calls `record_mcp_backoff_failure`; 5b's own defect is filed separately as
   `prespinal-gem-kinkajou` and pinned by a backoff-file-independence assertion in the new test.
2. T12 — asked how the gate behaves on an auth-enabled server. It is unaffected: the probe drives
   the session manager directly, never RequireAuthMiddleware, so an auth-enabled boot reports the
   same truthful transport result. Pinned by
   `test_an_auth_enabled_server_still_reports_a_successful_handshake`.
3. G6 — the strongest one: with the probe Host drawn from the allowlist, a WRONG-but-nonempty
   allowlist passes by construction, so the check could not catch the failure the ticket's own
   narrative describes. Probe-host precedence now starts from the deployment's DECLARED public
   resource URL (`REBAR_MCP_AUTH_RESOURCE_SERVER_URL`), which is declared independently of the
   allowlist, then falls back to a literal allowlist entry, a materialized `host:*`, and the bind.
   Pinned by `test_allowlist_that_admits_the_wrong_hostname_fails`.

Verification: 110 tests pass across the five affected modules; `make lint` and `make typecheck`
exit 0. Mutation check — 10 production edits reverted individually, each targeted test failing by
return code, every seed confirmed applied: probe-host precedence, the 200 status check, the
timeout scope, the lifespan ORDERING, the /health field, the `http.disconnect` in `receive` (the
observed hang), the lifespan wrap, the `run_http_with_grace` install call, the deploy-gate
predicate, and the backoff recorder. 10/10 killed. The install-call mutant initially SURVIVED —
the wiring line had no test — so
`test_run_http_with_grace_hands_uvicorn_an_app_that_runs_the_handshake` was added, which drives
the exact app handed to uvicorn through the raw ASGI lifespan.

Not closing: waiting on LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 on 2362.

compiled_state.description:
## Context

A 200 from `/health` does not establish that this container can serve an MCP request, yet it is
all the blue-green cutover waits for: the route sits OUTSIDE the auth middleware and the
DNS-rebinding guard (`src/rebar/_mcp_health.py`, `register_health_route`), and `autodeploy.sh`
flips the nginx upstream on a 200 without issuing one `/mcp` request (on the box 2026-08-28: a
container was promoted 54 s before serving its first). A container whose
`REBAR_MCP_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS` does not admit the hostname real traffic carries answers 200 while
421-ing every real request, and is promoted — the class of `mobile-groovy-badger`.

## Approach

Drive one real `initialize` through this server's own `StreamableHTTPSessionManager` inside the
ASGI lifespan — after the session manager runs, before Starlette answers
`lifespan.startup.complete` — and publish the outcome as a `handshake` object on `/health`.
Uvicorn accepts no connection until lifespan startup completes (Starlette's `Router.lifespan`
sends that message only after entering the context), so a later `/health` 200 proves by
construction that this container has already served an MCP handshake — which is why this is no
background task or lazy field.

**Conclusive.** The probe calls `mcp.session_manager.handle_request(scope, receive, send)` — the
entry point the `/mcp` route serves through (`StreamableHTTPASGIApp(self._session_manager)`,
`mcp/server/fastmcp/server.py:970`). A 200 needs the guard to admit the Host, the transport to
parse the body, the session manager to start a server task, and `Server.run` to answer. A
throwaway in-process probe on a `FastMCP` built like `build_server`'s returned 200 in 3.0 ms
admitting, 421 in 2.1 ms non-admitting. Boundary: calling the session manager directly does not
traverse `RequireAuthMiddleware`/`ProxyAuthMiddleware` (the server holds no credential to present
to itself), so an auth-enabled boot is UNAFFECTED — same truthful result (pinned by an AC), and
the gate cannot freeze it. This proves the transport + protocol path, not auth config.

**Bounded.** The drive runs under `anyio.fail_after(budget)` with module constant
`DEFAULT_HANDSHAKE_BUDGET_SECONDS = 10`, wrapped so a `TimeoutError`, any `Exception`, or a
non-200 status is a reported failure record, not a raise; boot continues. The timeout scope and
clock are injected — the `drain_then_exit(..., sleep=, monotonic=)` seam — so the bound is
provable with a fake clock, not by sleeping.

**Probe Host** (`select_probe_host`), in precedence, from this server's OWN settings: (1) the host
of the declared public resource URL, `mcp.settings.auth.resource_server_url`
(`REBAR_MCP_AUTH_RESOURCE_SERVER_URL`; on the box `https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp`,
`docker-compose.yml:400`), port appended only when not the scheme default — declared INDEPENDENTLY
of the allowlist, so an allowlist admitting a DIFFERENT hostname is caught with a 421: the
deploy-promotes-a-421-container case; (2) else the first literal `allowed_hosts` entry; (3) else
the first `host:*` entry as `host:<bind port>`, the form `_validate_host` matches; (4) else the bind address, `0.0.0.0`/`::` -> `127.0.0.1` —
where an allowlist admitting nothing usable (empty, or only unmatchable forms like
`*.example.com`) lands, then refused by its own guard. LIMIT: with no declared resource URL
nothing independent checks the allowlist, so a pass then proves the request path works, not that
the right hosts are admitted.

The deploy gate closes like the store gate (`autodeploy.sh` 5b): after `/health` 200, refuse the
flip when `handshake.ok` is present and false; an absent field promotes (mixed-version safety, as
the `store` gate treats an older container). The refusal calls `record_mcp_backoff_failure`, NOT
the `record_backoff_failure` 5b uses: `$BACKOFF_FILE` gates the whole script, so recording there
lets an mcp failure suppress the review-bot deploy (`autodeploy.sh:64-69`). 5b's own wrong
recorder is a separate defect, `prespinal-gem-kinkajou`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py` — `select_probe_host`, the ASGI drive, the bounded never-raising
  `run_startup_handshake`, `install_startup_handshake` (wraps `app.router.lifespan_context`,
  unwrapping any `ProxyAuthMiddleware`), the `handshake` field on `/health`, and its call from
  `run_http_with_grace`. 463 LOC today, under the 800 cap.
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_health_startup_handshake.py` — the unit tests.
- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py` — the `handshake` key + auth case.
- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` — readiness gate on `handshake.ok`.
- `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py` — deploy-gate tests on the `mcp_box` harness,
  which stubs per-port `/health`.
- `tests/unit/test_mcp_opcert_signing_goose.py:441` — the other direct `run_http_with_grace`
  caller, UNCHANGED by design: install is a guarded no-op when the app has no `.router` (its fake
  returns a bare `object()`) and reads `settings.auth` defensively. Run with the affected modules;
  an AC pins the guard.

No new config key: the budget is a module constant, per the `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS`
rationale.

## Testing

Every assertion is anchored: each test proves the handshake actually RAN (a drive counter, or the
record's presence) before asserting its outcome — an assertion that passes when it never ran is
this bug restated. Both directions are covered, the bound uses an injected clock not a sleep, and
each production edit is reverted with its targeted test required to fail (rc checked).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A correctly configured server reports a successful startup handshake on `/health`:
      `test_correctly_configured_server_reports_a_successful_handshake` asserts the drive counter
      incremented, record `{"ok": True, "status": 200}`.

- [ ] A server whose host allowlist does not admit its own probe reports the handshake failed
      with the refusing status instead of ready:
      `test_unadmitted_probe_host_is_reported_as_failed_with_421` asserts `ok is False`,
      `status == 421`.
- [ ] A handshake exceeding its budget is a reported failure and boot continues:
      `test_a_hanging_drive_is_bounded_by_the_budget` (injected clock, no sleep) asserts a record
      naming the timeout.
- [ ] A handshake whose drive raises never propagates it:
      `test_a_raising_drive_is_reported_not_propagated` asserts the record carries the message,
      the lifespan still yielding.
- [ ] The handshake completes inside the ASGI lifespan before uvicorn accepts a connection:
      `test_handshake_is_recorded_before_lifespan_startup_complete` drives the raw lifespan
      protocol, asserting the record exists before `lifespan.startup.complete` is sent.
- [ ] An auth-enabled server still reports a successful handshake, so the gate cannot freeze its
      deploys: `test_an_auth_enabled_server_still_reports_a_successful_handshake` asserts
      `ok is True` with a verifier configured.
- [ ] The cutover refuses a container reporting a failed handshake:
      `test_failed_handshake_container_is_not_promoted` asserts `mcp-handshake-failed` logged,
      upstream byte-identical, nginx not reloaded, container removed.
- [ ] A container whose `/health` predates the field is still promoted (mixed-version safety):
      `test_container_with_no_handshake_field_still_promotes` asserts the flip.
- [ ] A server whose allowlist admits a hostname OTHER than its declared public resource URL
      reports the handshake failed: `test_allowlist_that_admits_the_wrong_hostname_fails` asserts
      `ok is False`, 421.
- [ ] Installing against a server with no Starlette app / no auth settings never raises:
      `test_install_is_a_no_op_without_a_starlette_app`, plus
      `tests/unit/test_mcp_opcert_signing_goose.py` unchanged and passing.
- [ ] `make lint` exits 0.
- [ ] `make typecheck` passes.
- [ ] The affected tests pass.
- [ ] Each production edit reverted individually makes its targeted test fail (rc checked).

file_impact.reason: startup MCP handshake: probe-host selection, bounded never-raising drive, lifespan install, /health handshake field
new unit tests: positive, wrong-hostname and unadmitted-host negatives, injected-clock bound, never-raises, lifespan ordering, install no-op guard, probe-host precedence
pin the /health handshake key and the auth-enabled case through the real build_server
blue-green readiness gate refuses a container reporting handshake.ok=false, recording the mcp backoff (not the review-bot one)
deploy-gate tests for failed/ok/absent handshake field plus the backoff-file independence assertion
